  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object

        type:

          type: string

        title:
          title: Title

          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true

          title: Timestamp

          type: string
          format: date-time

          readOnly: true

          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:

          type: string

      required:

      properties:
        firstName:

          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a leading '+' with
            its country code is kept, otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a
            single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits. The result must be
            a '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits, and is stored and returned in that form.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be a
            syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
            Optional; when omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Create-time directive only. When true, allows creating this owner even though
            another owner already has the same lastName and address (they share a household);
            otherwise such a duplicate is rejected with 409 Conflict. Not stored or returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: true

              example: 1

              readOnly: true

## Summary

I implemented the `namesakeCount` field on owner creation. When a new owner is created via `POST /api/owners`, the response (and subsequent `GET /api/owners/{id}`) now includes `namesakeCount` = the number of owners that already existed *before* this create sharing the same `firstName` and `lastName`, compared case-insensitively.

Changes:

1. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — computes the count before saving the new owner and sets it on the entity, via a new `countNamesakes(firstName, lastName)` helper that scans existing owners with a null-safe case-insensitive comparison. It's computed before `saveOwner`, so it reflects only pre-existing owners.

2. **`Owner` entity** — added the persisted `namesakeCount` field (`namesake_count` column) with getter/setter, following the existing pattern of `customerCode`/`householdId`.

3. **`openapi.yml`** — added `namesakeCount` as a `readOnly` int32 property on the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` carries it and MapStruct maps it by name automatically.

4. **Schema SQL** (hsqldb/h2/mysql/postgres) — added the `namesake_count` column to the `owners` table so the entity persists and reads back correctly. The tests run on hsqldb.

The value is persisted at create time so the household/duplicate rules are unaffected, and reading the owner back returns the snapshot count as the test expects (owner "b" returns `namesakeCount = 1` after "a" with the same name was created first).
